text:
samira: heads up — support just escalated a couple of customers hitting 401s + aggressive client retries after the regenerated SDKs went out this morning. they see auth failing intermittently and then long retry loops that cause billing spikes. @devon can you triage?

support: adding context — both customers on dedicated infra, started after our client package updates. logged 401s from backend; request payloads look identical but headers differ between python vs ts clients. attached logs in the ticket. :grimacing:

maria: quick note — we rotated an OpenAPI spec patch yesterday that renamed the security scheme id from `api_key` -> `bearerAuth`. regenerated clients in CI used the new name, but I think the python generator kept sending `x-api-key` header while TS client switched to `Authorization: Bearer ...`. that mismatch would definitely 401.

samira: repro steps from support (minimal):
```
# ts client (broken)
fetch("https://api.redwood.example/v1/items", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer $TOKEN" } })
# python client (broken)
requests.get("https://api.redwood.example/v1/items", headers={"x-api-key": TOKEN})
```
they say our gateway requires `Authorization` for these customers, so python clients are failing.

devon: :eyes: ok. is this a generator bug or a CI/regeneration race? did the regen job bump the clients without a changelog entry?

ci-bot: regen-job #742 finished — generated clients (python@main, ts@main, go@main) from OpenAPI commit `f3a9b2`. No manual changelog provided.

maria: yep — the OpenAPI change was intentional (we standardized on `bearerAuth`) but the python template mapping wasn't updated in the generator, so it defaulted to the old header param name. that explains the mismatch.

tj: impact note from support: two customers hit hundreds of retries in 2 hours until they downgraded to previous pinned client. cost spike ~30% for those tenants. we should consider hotfixing generator + publishing patched packages and patching the regen CI to fail if security scheme id changes without manual review.

devon: immediate plan —
1) patch generator template so python emits `Authorization: Bearer` for `bearerAuth` scheme (I'll open PR now).
2) publish hotfix package releases: python 1.4.3, ts 2.8.1 with patched clients and tag in registry.
3) outreach: ping affected customers and ops to coordinate rollback or update.
4) add CI guard: fail regen if security scheme id changes or changelog empty.

support: FYI ticket updated with repro command and suggestion to pin pre-regeneration versions. customers want ETA for fix.

maria: PR #768 opened — generator change + unit tests for security scheme mapping. also added a small post-regenerate test that lints for missing changelog entry.

devon: thanks — I'll cut the hotfix releases once CI passes. @support please hold customers on rollback instructions: `pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.2` or `npm i @redwood/sdk@2.8.0` until we've propagated.

samira: perfect. also let's add a short postmortem note in #postmortems once this is closed — action items on regen process and changelog policy. :white_check_mark:

support: acknowledged, will relay and keep thread updated.

ci-bot: release pipeline started for python 1.4.3 and ts 2.8.1 (job 9901).

devon: CI green. releasing hotfixes now. will post artifacts and changelog link once published.

support: customers notified. one confirmed downgrade worked and billing stabilized. thank you everyone.

samira: nice work — follow-up: let's add automated smoke for auth header parity across generated SDKs to avoid mismatch in future.
